transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess what brought me in is I don’t really feel like myself anymore. I’m just kind of… flat, you know? I don’t talk to people much, even when they’re right there. At work, the cleaning route—something I used to just do—it feels like I’m pushing a loaded cart uphill just to get started.

And the building has these long hallways, funny how you notice the floor wax smell more when it’s quiet… but, yeah, mostly I’ve just gone quiet. Like I’m there, but not really.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Yeah… sometimes. Mostly when I’m mopping after hours, when the place is empty and the lights make that buzzing sound—you know, those old hallway lights, they never fix them right.

I’ll hear a man’s voice say my name, clear as anything, or say I missed a spot. Like he’s standing over by the stairwell. And I’ll turn and look, because it feels that close, but… there’s nobody there.
When the voice happens, do you feel depressed at those times?

Yeah… yeah, I think so. I mean, not every single time I hear it, maybe, but when I was really at the bottom—like barely eating, just feeling guilty about everything, even stupid things like not getting the trash liners folded right—I was hearing that man’s voice at work too.

That was also when I started feeling like people in the building were watching me. Like from the offices, or cameras maybe… I know buildings have cameras, of course, I clean around them all the time, little black domes in the corners. But it felt more personal than that. And I was having thoughts like… maybe I wouldn’t care if I didn’t wake up. So, yeah, the voice was happening when I was depressed like that.
Have you ever heard that voice during a time when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… there was a time like that, I think. A few weeks where I wasn’t so sunk down. I was eating a little more regular, getting through the route at work without standing there staring at the mop bucket forever.

But even then, I’d be in the stairwell and hear my name. Just my name, like someone calling from around the corner. And I still had it in my head that the hallway cameras weren’t just there for security… like they were being used to keep track of me specifically.

Those cameras, they put them in those little smoked domes, you know, and you can’t tell which way they’re pointing. I used to clean under them and try not to look up too much. But yeah… that was when I wasn’t feeling as depressed as before.
Was there ever a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing the voice or felt the cameras were tracking you, while you were not depressed?

Yeah… I think so. It wasn’t just a day or two. It was, I don’t know, several weeks maybe, where I wasn’t in that deep hole like before.

I was eating meals more regular, getting through work a little better… still slow, but not just standing there useless. But I’d still hear my name in the stairwell, clear enough that I’d stop and look.

And the cameras… those hallway cameras, with the dark little domes, I still felt like they were tracking me in particular. Not just normal security. I know that sounds… but yeah, that went on while I wasn’t feeling so depressed.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or high, much more than normal?

Unusually energetic or high… I don’t know. I don’t think I get “high” like that, not like bouncing off the walls or anything.

Sometimes if I get a decent night’s sleep, I can move a little faster at work, you know, get the trash pulled before the offices start filling up. But that’s not… I mean, that’s just having a better day. The floors take forever when people track in salt in the winter, and then you’re going over the same spot again and again—

Sorry. I guess I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I haven’t really noticed a time where I felt way more energetic than normal.
During those low periods, did you lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… yeah, I did. Things just kind of went flat.

I used to look forward to fishing on Saturdays, even if I didn’t catch much. Just sitting there with the line out, coffee in the thermos… there’s a spot where the weeds always snag if you cast too far left, and I knew that, I liked knowing that. But during those low times I’d just let the gear sit.

Same with crosswords in the morning. I used to do them with coffee, pencil all chewed up, you know. Or at work, showing the younger guys little tricks for stripping a floor so they don’t gouge it up. I used to get something out of that.

But lately… or during those times, I mostly just let those things sit. They don’t really give me anything back.
Have there been times when your depressed mood lasted most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 2 weeks?

Yeah… yes. It wasn’t just a rough weekend or something.

The low mood has been there most of the day, pretty much nearly every day, for… about a year and a couple months now, I think. It started not too long after I moved. I remember because I still had boxes stacked in the corner, and I kept telling myself I’d unpack them once I felt settled, but then weeks just kept going by.

So yeah, definitely more than two weeks. It’s been around a year and two months, give or take.
During the time you were hearing the voice or felt the cameras were tracking you, was there ever a period when those experiences were happening but you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yeah… there was a stretch like that, I think.

It wasn’t like I was cheerful exactly, but my mood had lifted some. I was getting through meals a little better, and work didn’t feel quite as impossible. I could get through my shift, do the stairwells, the hallway floors… you know, those cameras are in every hallway now, and some of them have that little red light—well, I guess not all of them do.

But even then, when I wasn’t feeling so depressed, I still heard my name in the stairwell. And I still felt sure the hallway cameras were being used to track me. So… yeah, it wasn’t only when I was really low.
Have the voice and the feeling that the cameras were tracking you been going on for at least 6 months continuously?

Yeah… I’d say so. It’s been about 11 months now, the voice and that feeling with the cameras.

I remember because I kept thinking it was just the building, you know, the way sound carries in stairwells. Those stairwells echo funny after they wax the floors, and the cameras—well, they’re everywhere now, even in grocery stores. But… no, it’s been going on pretty steady for around 11 months.
During that stretch when you still heard the voice and felt tracked by the cameras, were you free of depression completely?

Completely free? No… I don’t think I’d say completely.

There were several weeks where my mood had lifted some. Like, I was eating a little better, and getting through work didn’t feel quite so impossible. I could do the hallways and the stairwells without dragging myself as much… though the stairwells are where I’d still hear my name sometimes.

And the cameras, too — I still felt sure they were tracking me in the hallways, even during that better stretch. So I wasn’t as depressed then, but I wouldn’t say I was totally free of it.
Was there ever a time lasting at least 2 weeks when you heard the voice or felt tracked by the cameras while you were not depressed at all?

I don’t know if I’d say not depressed at all. There were several weeks where I was… better, I guess. Like I could eat more regular, and getting through work wasn’t such a mountain. I’d do the hallways, mop around the stairwells, and I wasn’t dragging as bad.

But the voice was still there sometimes — hearing my name in the stairwell. And I still felt like the hallway cameras were tracking me. Those cameras are everywhere now, and some of them are aimed at odd angles, like not where you’d expect… but yeah, even when my mood had lifted, that part didn’t really stop.
During those low periods, were you sleeping much less or much more than usual?

I’m not really sure… I didn’t keep track of it like that.

Some nights felt different than others, but with the cleaning work, the hours and the building routine kind of blur together. You know, you finish one floor and then another, and by the time you get home it’s hard to tell what’s “usual” anymore. So… I can’t say for sure if it was much less or much more.
At any time since the voice and the camera-tracking feeling started, were you completely free of depression for at least 2 weeks while those experiences were still happening?

I don’t think I was completely free of it, no. There was a stretch of several weeks where I was doing better — I was eating more normal, getting through my work a little easier, not feeling so weighed down every minute.

But the voice was still happening, like hearing my name in the stairwell, and I still believed the hallway cameras were tracking me. Those hallways have cameras in such strange spots, you know, and when you’re cleaning at night you notice all that. So… better mood, yes, but not totally free of depression.
During those low periods, did you feel down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so, most of the time. Since the move, it’s like that sadness and low energy were just kind of sitting there in the background. Even on days when I was more caught up worrying about the cameras or hearing things, the down feeling was still there underneath.

I’d be doing the cleaning, taking out trash, checking the same hallway lights, and it’s funny what you notice in buildings after hours… but yeah, the guilt and not really enjoying much of anything, that was there a lot. Nearly every day, I’d say, or close to it.
During those low periods, was your appetite decreased?

Yeah… I’d say it was decreased. Most days food just didn’t seem like food, more like cardboard or paper. I’d get home after the shift and maybe eat a few crackers, or just skip it because it felt like too much trouble.

And then I’d notice my work pants hanging looser, which—those pants are already cheap and the waistband never sits right, the kind they give you with those scratchy seams—but yeah, looser than they used to be. So I think I wasn’t eating much.
Before this current year-long low period began, had you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least 2 weeks?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, sure, but whether it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two whole weeks… I don’t know. Time gets blurry when you look back like that.

There were times years ago where I felt low, but I was still going to work and doing what I had to do. Then again, work can cover things up — you mop a floor, empty bins, keep moving, and the day goes by. Some buildings have those old buzzing lights, and that kind of thing can get under your skin after a while…

But, uh, before this past year? I can’t say for sure that there was another period like that. I don’t really know.
Before this past year, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least 2 weeks?

I’m… I’m not sure. I know I had times before where I felt pretty low, but pinning it down to “nearly every day” and “at least two weeks” is hard for me.

I remember certain jobs feeling heavier than others, especially in older buildings where the heat pipes knock and the floors never really get clean no matter how many times you go over them… but whether that was depression every day or just being worn down, I don’t know.

So before this past year, I can’t really say for sure that it happened like that.
Since this low mood started, has there ever been a period of at least 2 months when you were not depressed?

No… I don’t think there’s been a full two months where it lifted. It’s been pretty much with me since not long after I moved, about a year and two months now.

I mean, some days are a little less heavy than others, like if the weather’s decent or the building is quiet and nobody’s tracking mud everywhere, but that’s not the same as being not depressed. It never really went away for a couple months or anything like that.

patient.answer:

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking how long the voice and camera-tracking beliefs have been going on, which matches the duration of psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I’d say so. It’s been about 11 months now, the voice and that feeling with the cameras.

I remember because I kept thinking it was just the building, you know, the way sound carries in stairwells. Those stairwells echo funny after they wax the floors, and the cameras—well, they’re everywhere now, even in grocery stores. But… no, it’s been going on pretty steady for around 11 months.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms occur in the absence of any mood syndrome, which would favor schizophrenia over schizoaffective disorder or psychotic depression.
doctor.question: During that stretch when you still heard the voice and felt tracked by the cameras, were you free of depression completely?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a stretch of several weeks when my mood had lifted some and I was getting through meals and work a little better, but I still heard my name in the stairwell and stayed convinced the hallway cameras were being used to track me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the psychotic symptoms occurred during a stretch when depression was completely absent, which directly assesses psychotic symptoms in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Completely free? No… I don’t think I’d say completely.

There were several weeks where my mood had lifted some. Like, I was eating a little better, and getting through work didn’t feel quite so impossible. I could do the hallways and the stairwells without dragging myself as much… though the stairwells are where I’d still hear my name sometimes.

And the cameras, too — I still felt sure they were tracking me in the hallways, even during that better stretch. So I wasn’t as depressed then, but I wouldn’t say I was totally free of it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a period of at least 2 weeks with psychotic symptoms in the complete absence of depression, which would distinguish schizoaffective disorder from psychotic depression and help separate it from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Was there ever a time lasting at least 2 weeks when you heard the voice or felt tracked by the cameras while you were not depressed at all?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a stretch of several weeks when my mood had lifted some and I was getting through meals and work a little better, but I still heard my name in the stairwell and stayed convinced the hallway cameras were being used to track me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether there was a period of at least 2 weeks when hallucinations or delusions occurred without depression, which directly matches this item.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d say not depressed at all. There were several weeks where I was… better, I guess. Like I could eat more regular, and getting through work wasn’t such a mountain. I’d do the hallways, mop around the stairwells, and I wasn’t dragging as bad.

But the voice was still there sometimes — hearing my name in the stairwell. And I still felt like the hallway cameras were tracking me. Those cameras are everywhere now, and some of them are aimed at odd angles, like not where you’d expect… but yeah, even when my mood had lifted, that part didn’t really stop.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode meets full major depressive episode criteria by assessing sleep disturbance, which helps distinguish schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder from psychotic major depression.
doctor.question: During those low periods, were you sleeping much less or much more than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about sleep changes (sleeping much less or much more), but the provided symptom profile does not include a sleep disturbance item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure… I didn’t keep track of it like that.

Some nights felt different than others, but with the cleaning work, the hours and the building routine kind of blur together. You know, you finish one floor and then another, and by the time you get home it’s hard to tell what’s “usual” anymore. So… I can’t say for sure if it was much less or much more.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms have persisted in the absence of a major depressive episode long enough to distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder or psychotic depression.
doctor.question: At any time since the voice and the camera-tracking feeling started, were you completely free of depression for at least 2 weeks while those experiences were still happening?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a stretch of several weeks when my mood had lifted some and I was getting through meals and work a little better, but I still heard my name in the stairwell and stayed convinced the hallway cameras were being used to track me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether hallucinations/delusional camera-tracking experiences continued for at least 2 weeks while completely free of depression, which directly matches Criterion B.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I was completely free of it, no. There was a stretch of several weeks where I was doing better — I was eating more normal, getting through my work a little easier, not feeling so weighed down every minute.

But the voice was still happening, like hearing my name in the stairwell, and I still believed the hallway cameras were tracking me. Those hallways have cameras in such strange spots, you know, and when you’re cleaning at night you notice all that. So… better mood, yes, but not totally free of depression.

inference.note: Ruled out F20.9 because psychotic symptoms have not occurred for at least 2 weeks in the complete absence of depressive symptoms; psychosis persists only when depression is present or partially remitted. Schizoaffective depressive type remains most likely because psychosis lasted weeks when not in a major depressive episode, though not entirely depression-free.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had a distinct major depressive episode with a core symptom required for major depression, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia with depressive symptoms and major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: During those low periods, did you feel down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: For most of the time since the move, the sadness, low energy, guilt, and loss of interest have been there in the background, even on days when the voices or camera worries were the main thing on my mind.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the persistence and frequency of depressed mood during low periods, which is most directly covered by the profile describing the depressive episode being present for most of the illness, with sadness and related depressive symptoms in the background.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so, most of the time. Since the move, it’s like that sadness and low energy were just kind of sitting there in the background. Even on days when I was more caught up worrying about the cameras or hearing things, the down feeling was still there underneath.

I’d be doing the cleaning, taking out trash, checking the same hallway lights, and it’s funny what you notice in buildings after hours… but yeah, the guilt and not really enjoying much of anything, that was there a lot. Nearly every day, I’d say, or close to it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode includes a key neurovegetative symptom to confirm a major depressive episode rather than depressive symptoms secondary to schizophrenia-spectrum illness.
doctor.question: During those low periods, was your appetite decreased?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Most days food just tastes like cardboard, so I skip meals or eat a few crackers after my shift, and my work pants have been hanging looser than they used to.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether appetite was decreased during low periods, which matches appetite and weight changes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I’d say it was decreased. Most days food just didn’t seem like food, more like cardboard or paper. I’d get home after the shift and maybe eat a few crackers, or just skip it because it felt like too much trouble.

And then I’d notice my work pants hanging looser, which—those pants are already cheap and the waistband never sits right, the kind they give you with those scratchy seams—but yeah, looser than they used to be. So I think I wasn’t eating much.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has a history of prior separate depressive episodes, which would distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder with psychotic features from a single severe depressive episode with psychotic features, given that schizoaffective disorder is less likely because there was no 2-week period of psychosis without any depression.
doctor.question: Before this current year-long low period began, had you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least 2 weeks?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a prior lifetime depressive episode before the current year-long low period, but the provided profile only covers the current depressive episode and its duration, not any earlier episodes.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, sure, but whether it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two whole weeks… I don’t know. Time gets blurry when you look back like that.

There were times years ago where I felt low, but I was still going to work and doing what I had to do. Then again, work can cover things up — you mop a floor, empty bins, keep moving, and the day goes by. Some buildings have those old buzzing lights, and that kind of thing can get under your skin after a while…

But, uh, before this past year? I can’t say for sure that there was another period like that. I don’t really know.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was any past distinct major depressive episode before the current one, to distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder with psychotic features (F33.3) from single-episode major depressive disorder with psychotic features (F32.3), given schizoaffective disorder is less likely because psychosis has not occurred during a period completely free of depression.
doctor.question: Before this past year, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least 2 weeks?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a prior depressive episode before the current year-long period, but the provided symptom profile only specifies the current depressive episode duration and symptoms, not whether there was a separate earlier episode.

patient.answer:
I’m… I’m not sure. I know I had times before where I felt pretty low, but pinning it down to “nearly every day” and “at least two weeks” is hard for me.

I remember certain jobs feeling heavier than others, especially in older buildings where the heat pipes knock and the floors never really get clean no matter how many times you go over them… but whether that was depression every day or just being worn down, I don’t know.

So before this past year, I can’t really say for sure that it happened like that.

inference.note: Persistent psychotic symptoms occur only during periods of ongoing depression or partial remission, with no clear ≥2-week period completely free of depression while psychosis persists. This rules against F25.1 requiring at least 2 weeks of psychosis without mood symptoms, and prior episodes are not established, making F33.3 less supported than F32.3.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive syndrome has been present continuously for at least 2 years, which would support schizoaffective disorder depressive type over major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Since this low mood started, has there ever been a period of at least 2 months when you were not depressed?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depression part has been with me for about 1 year and 2 months, starting not long after the move.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the continuity and duration of the depressive episode since the low mood began, specifically whether there was a 2-month remission period.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think there’s been a full two months where it lifted. It’s been pretty much with me since not long after I moved, about a year and two months now.

I mean, some days are a little less heavy than others, like if the weather’s decent or the building is quiet and nobody’s tracking mud everywhere, but that’s not the same as being not depressed. It never really went away for a couple months or anything like that.

inference.note: Persistent depressive symptoms for ~14 months without a 2-month remission, plus psychotic symptoms for ~11 months. Psychosis also occurred during periods when depression was only partially improved, but there was no clear >=2-week period completely free of depression while psychosis persisted, ruling against F32.3 and supporting schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusional beliefs) for about 11 months together with a major depressive syndrome lasting about 14 months. There were several weeks of psychotic symptoms when depression was less intense, but the interview did not establish a period of at least 2 weeks of psychosis in the complete absence of mood symptoms. There is no history of mania/hypomania. The picture is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, among the provided candidates.
